problem_statement: adrianhajdin/gsap_macbook_landing is a Vite + React + GSAP + three.js single-page marketing landing for the MacBook Pro. It scroll-animates a pinned hero, a live three.js product viewer whose finish (Silver / Space Black) and display size (14-inch / 16-inch) are held in a shared zustand store, a GSAP showcase, a performance product-shot deck, a features canvas, a highlights masonry, and a footer. Below the highlights the landing hosts its 'Configure your MacBook Pro' configurator: a finish chip row, a display-size chip row, a live 'Configured: MacBook Pro <size> · <finish> · from $<price>' readout, and a summary rail of tiles (Selected finish, Selected size, Starting price, Viewer angle). The configurator writes to the same store that drives the viewer, and a compact copy of the configuration is echoed a second time as a footer proof rail before the shop links, so the chosen build stays visible at the point of checkout. The configurator asset shipped with several regressions: (1) the finish and size chip rows and the summary rail are pinned to a fixed-width, flex-wrap:nowrap track of fixed-width chips/tiles, so on a 390px phone the configurator runs off the right edge and pushes the whole landing into horizontal scrolling; (2) the chip and tile tracks collide — chips shingle on top of each other and over the configuration readout while the summary tiles overlap into an unreadable band, so the panel looks broken on desktop; (3) the footer proof rail that should re-surface the configuration before the shop links is missing; and (4) the configuration readout and summary are captured once at mount and never re-derived, so picking a different finish or size updates the viewer and the active chip but leaves the readout frozen on the default build. Repair the configurator so it lays out responsively with no horizontal overflow at 390px, the chips/tiles/readout no longer overlap and stay legible on desktop and tablet, the footer proof rail is present and reflects the current build, and the readout and summary update live whenever a finish or size is chosen — while the surrounding hero, live product viewer, showcase, performance, features, highlights, and footer stay intact and reachable.
required_content: The landing keeps the 'Configure your MacBook Pro' configurator with its finish chips (Silver, Space Black), display-size chips (14-inch, 16-inch), the live configuration readout, and the summary tiles (Selected finish, Selected size, Starting price, Viewer angle).
At 390px the landing no longer overflows horizontally: the finish/size chip rows and the summary rail wrap or shrink so the document width stays within the phone viewport.
On desktop and tablet the chips, summary tiles, and configuration readout lay out without overlapping or being clipped, so every chip label, tile value, and the readout stay legible.
The footer proof rail that re-surfaces the current MacBook configuration before the shop links is present and reflects the selected finish and size.
Choosing a finish or a display size updates the live configuration readout and the summary tiles in lockstep with the three.js viewer, rather than leaving them frozen on the default build.
The surrounding landing sections (navigation, hero, live product viewer with its color/size controls, showcase, performance, features, highlights, footer) remain intact and reachable.
design_constraints: Preserve the MacBook landing design language: the dark Apple-style palette, the rounded card/chip look, the centered section heading rhythm, and the local OTF typography.
Keep the configurator wired to the existing zustand store that drives the live three.js product viewer; do not fork the finish/size state or break the viewer's own color/size controls.
Fix the configurator layout and the stale-readout wiring only; do not delete the configurator, its chips, the readout, the summary tiles, the footer proof rail, or the live product viewer.

Keep the configurator built from the existing component pattern under src/components (MacConfig.jsx, ConfigProof.jsx) mounted in src/App.jsx; the responsive and overlap fixes belong in src/components/macconfig.css and the live-readout fix in the component.
Do not introduce external fonts, remote stock imagery, analytics, or CDN scripts; the landing must build with Vite and run offline with a clean browser console.
state_constraints: desktop_configurator captures the landing scrolled to the 'Configure your MacBook Pro' panel on a 1440px desktop: the finish/size chips and summary tiles lay out cleanly without overlapping and every label is readable.
mobile_configurator captures the same configurator at 390px, where the baseline/bad fixed-width nowrap chip tracks overflow the viewport and force the landing document into horizontal scrolling.
tablet_configurator captures the configurator at 834px as an intermediate viewport where the reference stays within tolerance while the broken tracks still overflow.

desktop_config_default captures the configurator before any selection (default 16-inch · Space Black); desktop_config_silver14 captures it after clicking the 14-inch size chip and the Silver finish chip, where the readout must now read '14-inch · Silver'.
desktop_footer captures the footer proof rail region that re-surfaces the current configuration; it is present in the reference and absent when the footer proof rail is dropped.

Source inspection confirms the configurator is a self-contained component (src/components/MacConfig.jsx + ConfigProof.jsx) whose layout lives in src/components/macconfig.css, so the fixes are isolated to those files.

change_completion: The configurator keeps its finish chips, size chips, live readout, and summary tiles.
The mobile landing no longer overflows horizontally; the chip rows and summary rail reflow to fit 390px.
Choosing a finish or size updates the readout and summary live, in lockstep with the viewer.
The footer proof rail is present and reflects the current build.
design_consistency: The fix preserves the MacBook landing dark palette, the chip/tile card look, and the section heading rhythm.
The chips, tiles, and readout no longer overlap or clip; the panel reads as a coherent configurator.
No other landing section or the live product viewer is restyled.
regression: The Vite build still serves as a static site without a custom dev server beyond a static file host.
The hero, live product viewer with its color/size controls, and every other section remain reachable.
responsive: 390px landing has no horizontal overflow after the fix.
The configurator chips and summary tiles wrap or shrink cleanly on mobile instead of overflowing.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Vite + React + GSAP + three.js MacBook Pro marketing-landing repair. The native lever is the landing's own 'Configure your MacBook Pro' configurator, wired to the same zustand store that drives the live three.js product viewer (finish + display size). Four orthogonal defects on the shipped configurator asset: a fixed-width flex-nowrap chip/tile track that overflows a 390px phone (no_horizontal_overflow); shingled chips/tiles that overlap the readout and each other into an illegible panel on desktop (visual_regression on the configurator crops); a dropped footer proof rail so the configuration is only surfaced once (dom_assertions on the footer-scoped proof rail); and a readout/summary snapshotted at mount so picking a finish or size updates the viewer and the active chip but leaves the readout frozen on the default build (interaction_assertions). The reference repairs all four: the chip rows and summary rail flex-wrap and shrink so mobile overflow is eliminated, the chips/tiles/readout no longer collide, the footer proof rail is restored, and the readout/summary derive live from the store. The three legs differ only in src/components/MacConfig.jsx, macconfig.css, and ConfigProof.jsx; the global overflow-x clip and the pre-existing GSAP/media sections are neutralized identically across all three legs as declared build infrastructure so the only measurable overflow is the configurator itself. Local OTF fonts, MacBook Pro product imagery under public/, and the dark Apple-style palette are preserved.
